Prevention: Spiders, Dragon flies, Ladybird beetles, Predatory wasps and
Parasitic wasps through conservation of patches of natural vegetation.
Plant early in the season at the onset of rains.Plant companion crops such as marigold and geraniums around the rice field.
Control weeds in the field to remove the preferred grassy hosts of
Rotate rice with non-grass crops like potatoes, cabbages, soya beans, beans etc.
Avoid overlap/relay planting of rice crop.
Reduce the number of rice crops to two per year and synchronize crop establishment across farms to reduce leafhoppers infestations.
Avoid planting during the peak of leafhopper activity (shown by historical records) to avoid infestation.
Transplant older seedlings (>3 weeks) to reduce susceptibility to viral diseases transmitted by leafhoppers.
Monitoring: Inspect regularly for slender, wedge-shaped insects with varying body colors of green, yellow, brown and are often mottled, mostly matching the colour of the host plant.
Look for light-colored speckling on plant leaves that gradually lead to browning of the leaves.
Inspect young plants or new growth for stunted growth and/or deformations.
Inspect shoots for curls and/ or dying while the tips of infested leaves develop diamond- shape yellowing, may also appear stippled, pale or brown.
Use light traps to show leafhopper presence.
Take action when 3-5 nymphs per hill are seen.
Direct Control: Uproot infected plants and feed livestock or burn.
Control the leafhoppers by digging a trench between rice fields and planting grass on the bands.
